title: Anthropic reaches $65 billion in annualized revenue and launches invisible watermarks in Claude
summary: The AI startup reports explosive revenue growth while implementing watermarks in its outputs to combat misuse, though critics question privacy.

title: Amazon destroys rare books to train its AI, according to AirTag investigation
summary: An AirTag tracking reveals that Amazon sends scarce books to a facility dedicated to feeding AI models instead of selling them.

title: Workshops in China and Japan modify RTX 3080 and 2080 Ti graphics cards to 20-22 GB VRAM for AI workloads
summary: Amid VRAM scarcity and high prices, Asian markets offer modifications that double the memory of older GPUs, turning them into economical alternatives for AI.

title: Geekom distributes drivers with malware in its mini PCs and withdraws package after being discovered
summary: The company admits to shipping infected network drivers in its AMD mini PCs and publishes removal guide after security researchers' report.

title: Flock and AI cameras detect mobile phone use while driving in Spain and spark privacy debate in US
summary: While Catalonia fines thousands of drivers with smart cameras, in the United States fear grows over the expansion of the Flock surveillance network without improvement in crime resolution.

title: Judge authorizes Nine PBS to recover 70 years of television archive stored on Iron Mountain servers
summary: A court ruling confirms that the public broadcaster owns 50 TB of historical data following the collapse of its hosting provider.

title: Intel confirms its Nova Lake processors will arrive first on desktop with up to 28 cores and AVX-512
summary: Intel's next generation of CPUs will debut on desktop before laptops, with 24 and 28 core configurations and AVX-512 support enabled.
